title: STAR reflection — spoken follow-up
situation: In a technical discussion, an interviewer asks about a defect you introduced. You must answer aloud accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Say aloud how you introduced a defect, what it cost, and what you changed so it cannot recur.

vocabulary.meaning: an account of your own mistake that names the cost and the correction, without diluting responsibility across the team
the durable modification made after a defect, which is what distinguishes a lesson from an apology

expectedElements: The consequence is stated in measurable terms
A durable preventive change is described
modelAnswer: I introduced it. We were adding a filter to the order search, and I moved the pagination before the filter, which meant the second page could skip records. It reached production and it took two days before a customer noticed, which is the part I think about: nothing in our suite would have caught it. It affected roughly forty searches. What I changed afterwards is not that I am more careful, because that is not a control. I added a test that paginates a filtered set and asserts the total count across pages, which is now the evidence that the defect cannot return. That test would have failed on my change.
commonMistakes: Diluting responsibility across the team or the review process
Offering greater care as the preventive change instead of a control that fails
variants: Answer again for a defect that was caught before reaching production.
